title: How Blest Is He, Who Ne'er Consents
description: How Blest Is He, Who Ne'er Consents in Tonic Solfa to ST. PETER, doh is Eb: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Nahum Tate and Nicholas Brady wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 409 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “The Righteous and the Wicked”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST. PETER; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: How blest is he, who ne'er con-sents By ill ad-vice to walk; Nor stands in sin-ners' ways, nor sits Where men pro-fane-ly talk:

lines: How blest is he, who ne'er consents
Nor stands in sinners' ways, nor sits
But makes the perfect law of God
Like some fair tree, which, fed by streams,
He still shall flourish, and success

licence: Public domain: Nahum Tate died in 1715; Nicholas Brady died in 1726.
credits: Words by Nahum Tate (1652–1715) and Nicholas Brady (1659–1726), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to ST. PETER by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
